annotations.title: Portfolio scenarios: macro shocks and past crises

description: A portfolio's holdings under a macro shock or a past crisis. Shock some of eight factors (US stocks, the 2- and 10-year Treasury yields, the Baa-Aaa spread, oil, the dollar, gold, the VIX) and the rest move as history says they do alongside, with a 90% range; or replay a crisis (2008, 2020, 2022 and eight more) beside each holding's actual return then, with the model's error. Betas from weekly returns over the last years. Local server (prices).

holdings.description: The portfolio, up to 25 holdings. Weights are used as given: they need not sum to 1 (a hedged book can sum to 0).

symbol.description: A stock, ETF or fund as price_history reads it (AAPL, TLT, SAP.DE).

weight.description: Its share of the portfolio's value as a fraction (0.25 is a quarter; negative for a short).

horizon_weeks.description: Weeks a hypothetical shock plays out over, which sets the range around the answer. Default 4.

portfolio_value.description: The portfolio's value, to give the results in money too.

scenario.description: A past crisis to replay instead of shocks: dotcom_bust, bank_crisis, debt_ceiling_2011, taper_tantrum, oil_collapse, dollar_surge, q4_2018, pandemic_crash, inflation_shock, compute_bust or regional_bank_run.

shocks.description: A hypothetical scenario: the factors you move. Those you leave out move by what history implies given yours.

credit_spread.description: The Baa-over-Aaa corporate spread's change in percentage points.

dollar.description: The broad dollar index's return, as a fraction.

equities.description: US stocks' return, as a fraction (-0.2 is a 20% fall).

oil.description: Oil's return, as a fraction (0.5 is a 50% rise).

rates_10y.description: The 10-year Treasury yield's change in percentage points.

rates_2y.description: The 2-year Treasury yield's change in percentage points (0.5 is 50 basis points).

volatility.description: The VIX's change in points (15 takes 20 to 35).

years.description: Years of weekly history the betas and the factors' covariance come from. Default 5.

name: scenario_risk

outputSchema.description: factors and holdings are tables (columns and rows); portfolio has the model's return with a 90% range for a shock, or the actual and replayed return for a crisis; model_check says how far a replay's model landed from what happened.

title: Portfolio scenarios: macro shocks and past crises
